title: Onset of the Middle Stone Age in Africa
summary: In the Olorgesailie basin of southern Kenya, people shifted around 320,000 years ago from large handaxes, used for hundreds of thousands of years, to smaller points and prepared cores. They obtained obsidian from 25 to 50 kilometres away and worked red pigment. These changes mark the earliest dated Middle Stone Age at this site.

uncertainty.note: Converted with year = 1950 minus years ago. Brooks et al. date the Olorgesailie Middle Stone Age sites to about 295,000-320,000 years ago; the Smithsonian page says people entered the Middle Stone Age from around 320,000 years ago. Onset elsewhere in Africa may differ.

as_recorded.value: Middle Stone Age sites dating from >=295,000 to ~320,000 years ago
Beginning around 320,000 years ago, people living there entered the Middle Stone Age

where.historical_name: Lake-basin landscape in the East African Rift, no polity

importance.justification: Shows a documented shift to more mobile, exchange-linked technology at the time Homo sapiens emerged in Africa.

reviewer_note: Dates are for Olorgesailie only; the Middle Stone Age is not a single event and other African sites (e.g. Jebel Irhoud) are covered in related records. Wikidata gives the site to two decimals only; uncertainty set to 10 km for the basin.
